Marathon Petroleum stock edged up 0.15% today to close at $396.52, continuing a two-week rally of 7.5% that reflects rising oil prices and tightening energy markets. Oil has climbed above $100 per barrel (now at $97.26 domestically, $109.51 globally) due to geopolitical tensions — Saudi Arabia shut a key pipeline bypassing the Strait of Hormuz after Iranian attacks, and U.S.-Iran hostilities have escalated. Refineries are running at 97.8% capacity, near maximum, which means the company benefits from both higher crude costs that it processes into refined products and tight supply conditions that support margins.

The regulatory environment has also shifted in the company's favor: the Trump administration repealed Obama and Biden-era greenhouse gas requirements for power plants on September 14, removing a headwind for fossil fuel producers. With prediction market traders now betting gas prices will hit new yearly highs, the refining sector is positioned to capture strong margins as long as crude remains elevated and demand stays firm.
